exposure: mode of surfactant administration (less invasive or INSURE technique vs. only after CPAP failure)
surfactant administration using less invasive or INSURE technique
outcome: incidence of continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) failure
cohort: 165 outborn very preterm infants (<32 weeks) with respiratory distress syndrome (RDS), initially managed on CPAP
finding: Early administration of surfactant using less invasive techniques in very preterm infants with RDS significantly reduced the probability of CPAP failure, which was strongly associated with increased morbidity and mortality.
mod_finding: This study focused on surfactant administration in preterm infants and did not directly compare modes of delivery.
